fields.title: Polka: the budget that doesn't add up
fields.summary: Speed target is 1.5 seconds, minimum possible time is 2.9 s. Main screen.
fields.decisionPrompt: How do we meet the budget? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are the Polka product manager.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are the Polka product manager. A new screen "Build cart in 2 minutes" — a selection of items based on the user's habitual purchases. Speed target is 1.5 s at p95, same as the main screen. The team says the minimum possible time is 2.9 s.
fields.brief/objective: Meet a reasonable time without paying for speed with a selection that is outdated by a day.
fields.brief/constraints: Target carried over from the main screen. Drop-off measured: up to 2 seconds is 5%.
fields.brief/task: Decide how you will meet the target and what you do with the goal.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: A speed target is also a hypothesis
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A number carried over from another screen does not become a requirement just because it is written in the task. Break down the budget into components, calculate what each fix provides, and compare the remaining gap with drop-off data. Sometimes the right move is not to hit the number at all costs, but to change the number by showing why the difference is worth nothing.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Profile and purchase history 180 ms. Personal selection (recommendation service) 900 ms. Stock check for 20 items 640 ms, 20 sequential calls. Prices 220 ms. Images of 20 items, 1.4 MB. Network and rendering 460 ms. Everything is sequential.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: "The selection can be pre-calculated at night — 4 days, but then it won't reflect today's purchases. Stock check via batch request — 2 days, drops to 90 ms. Prepared images — 3 days. Parallelization of independent calls — 3 days."
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: The screen is conceived as the main way to reorder. Expected to be used by 40% of returning users.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: On the main screen: up to 2 s — 5%, 2–4 s — 12%, more than 4 s — 28%.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: 12 days. Batch stock check, images, parallelization, pre-calculation of selection.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: fits the timeframe and likely the target. Pre-calculated selection at night misses today's purchases — noticeable for a grocery service: bought milk in the morning, still in the selection in the evening.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: time around 1.9 s. Target not met, but according to data, drop-off at 2 s is only 5%. Selection is up-to-date. Time buffer remains in the sprint.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Revise target to 2 s and do 8 days of work
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Revise target to 2 s and do 8 days of work. 8 days plus alignment.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: same as B, but the target is formally met. Requires justifying the revision with data.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Launch as is, optimize later. 0 days.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: 2.9 s, table drop-off around 12%. Screen is designed as the main reorder scenario — bad first impression on a key feature.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not build a budget along the critical path
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not apply the four levers in the correct order
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not verify the validity of the goal
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Caching is chosen without considering what the user pays for staleness
